aiOverview.content: The Artemis II Orion capsule successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET (0007 GMT April 11). This marked the safe return of four astronauts from a 10-day lunar mission, landing at approximately 20 mph after re-entering the atmosphere at 24,000 mph.Final Descent Sequence: The capsule, carrying astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen, underwent a "skip entry" maneuver to manage heat. Parachutes deployed to slow the craft to roughly 20 mph for a gentle splashdown.Recovery Operation: The crew was retrieved by the USS John P. Murtha (or via NBC News) using helicopters for extraction.Mission Significance: This was the first crewed lunar mission since 1972, with the capsule appearing on YouTube and on The New York Times.Future Missions: The SpaceX Crew-10 and upcoming SpaceX Crew-11 missions to the ISS have utilized similar parachute-assisted splashdowns in the same region, notes this YouTube video.
